sources.title: Concurrency Response of Plain Global Loads on the NVIDIA H100
sources.snippet: The bandwidth a memory-bound GPU kernel sustains is set by how many bytes it keeps in flight. We use Little's Law here as throughput accounting, not as a measured hardware pool. CUDA fills that budget on Hopper through plain loads (ld.global) and asynchronous copies (cp.async), among other paths; we characterize their concurrency response with clean-room microbenchmarks on three H100 SXM5 dies.
